text: CPI just hit 4.2% — a 3-year high — and the Fed is now signaling a possible rate hike later this year instead of cuts, which means borrowing costs could go up and that's bad news for cash-burning, speculative stocks in your portfolio.

RGTI is down 38% with revenue shrinking by 34%, nearly 19% short interest (meaning a lot of pros are betting against it), insiders are selling their own shares, and it's 65% below its high — this one is broken, get out.
QBTS is losing money, burning through cash, down 49% from its high with 17% short interest and insiders selling — there's no fundamental reason to hold this, take the loss and move on.

IONQ is another cash-burning quantum computing bet with negative earnings, 15%+ short interest, and insiders heading for the exits — in a rising-rate environment this kind of speculative stock gets hit hardest, so cut it now.

SGLP.L is your biggest position and it's down 20% with the worst relative strength score possible at -99 — even if you believe in it long-term, being this overweight a position that's performing this poorly is too much risk in one place.
GDX.L is down over 20% and 35% below its yearly high with bearish momentum, so reduce your exposure here and free up capital for stronger opportunities.
Adobe looks compelling at just 7x earnings with 10.5% revenue growth and outstanding cash flow — this pullback in a profitable, proven business is the kind of opportunity worth adding to gradually.
Google at 23.7x earnings with 15% revenue growth and insiders actually buying their own shares is a vote of confidence — consider adding a bit here while it's reasonably priced.
